notes.title: Monstro Goes Free and Open Source
notes.notes:
Mid September [b]Monstro[/b], along with its soundtrack, will become free on Steam. I will also release the sources for this game on GitHub - expect another announcement soon.

[h2]But why?[/h2]

It's really about three things: money, statement and [i]promoting[/i] my upcoming new release. So let's break it down!

[b]Money:[/b] I haven't earned anything from this game in years and while I don't mind it, it's a bit of a painful reminder of all the things I regret with this project. I had an offer or two of some suspicious people wanting to buy the game off me for some extra cash, but that's where the second part comes in.

[b]Statement:[/b] my qualms aside, it was still a project I invested considerable time into. While there is an amount of money I'd be willing to accept to part with it, it's not something anyone would offer for it. I want people to be able to play it. I want people to still have some last minute fun. So the next best thing is to set it free.

[b]Promoting:[/b] this is also an excuse to cross promote my upcoming game that's been in Early Access for a bit over a year. An excellent puzzle game Trans Neuronica which you can also find on Steam.

To everyone who played the game before - THANK YOU!

notes.title: Unit voices added in 1.0.4 and week-long discount starting Monday
notes.notes:
Monstro: Battle Tactics was just updated to 1.0.4 and among other things, thanks to a collaboration with [url=http://seespacelabs.com/]Seespace Labs[/url] units in Monstro now have voices (which you can conveniently disable if you find them not to your liking. The full changelog:
 - Unit voices added
 - "Wait for tap" is now by default disabled
 - "Wait for tap" should now react to all keys and mouse inputs
 - Pause menu can now be opened at all times
 - You can press "Q" from the victory/failure screen to quickly undo your last move without having to engage mouse
 - You can now press any key to skip/accelerate the victory/failure screen animation

In other [b]important[/b] news starting Monday we're running a week-long discount, so share the news with your friends!

notes.title: Quick 1.0.2 update
notes.notes:
We just posted a quick update to 1.0.2 which includes:
 - Ability to scroll using arrows
 - Option to toggle the old, drag'n'drop controls (experimental! It's possible there might be trivial bugs and visual glitches)
 - Sound effects volume now affects the dubbing in outros/intros
 - Retrocade logo volume is affected by  the music volume
 - Display Options have been added where you can more easily toggle between full-screen (it also informs you that you can use F10 for this)
 - Added a volume preview when changing sound volume

If by any chance you don't see/get the update immediately try the Verify Integrity of Game Cache option from Local Files tab in game's Properties window.

notes.title: Monstro: Battle Tactics is now officially released!
notes.notes:
We're extremely proud to announce that Monstro has been released on Steam! Don't wait to buy the game because the 10% discount will only last for the first week.

Have fun playing!

notes.title: Just how did Monstro change for Steam release?
notes.notes:
If you're new to Monstro: Battle Tactics you might not realize the game was originally released at the beginning of 2014. It's been almost two years since then and we've prepared a small comparison between then and now:

https://www.facebook.com/monstrobattletactics/photos/a.791303547644992.1073741828.789710874470926/791303074311706/

Hopefully it'll ease the pain of having to wait a bit over 9 more days for the game to be released!
